source_changes.before: An infinite expectation is allowed, so every measurable estimator has an extended nonnegative risk.
source_changes.after: An infinite expectation is allowed, so every measurable estimator has an extended nonnegative risk. Suprema of risks are taken in the ordered range $[0,\infty]$, with $\sup\varnothing:=0$, its least element. Thus when $\mathcal Q$ or $\mathcal P$ is empty the corresponding supremum is zero for every estimator, and its minimax risk is zero. The estimator class is nonempty because the constant zero matrix map is measurable.

source_changes.before: Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent identically distributed random vectors in $\mathbb R^p$
source_changes.after: Let $n,p\ge1$ be integers and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent identically distributed random vectors in $\mathbb R^p$
